Now you need to save humanity through space colonization... Welcome to the Moon uses the same flip-and-write game mechanisms as the earlier title Welcome To..., but now you can play in a campaign across eight adventure sheets. On a turn, you flip cards from three stacks to create three different combinations of a starship number and a corresponding action, then all players choose one of these three combinations. You use the number to fill a space in a zone on your adventure sheet in numerical order, and everyone is racing to be the first to complete common missions. The eight adventure sheets feature very different mechanisms from the classic Welcome To... concept, and when you play in campaign mode, you'll make choices that change the next adventure, which means that each campaign will differ from the previous one. [Rating: 1/10] J'avais noté 4 mais en fait autant mettre 1, et ils servaient pas de pop-corn dans la 6e navette, quelle honte !

[Rating: 1/10] What a waste. Theme is totally pasted-on, the gameplay is super abstract without incentive, immersion, and fun. It's just writing numbers. What the hell?

[Rating: 2/10] I do not understand all the buzz about this game. Reading and understanding the rules of every mission costs more time than playing. So far I had no fun at all. I can not see any strategic depth. And much worse, there is no fun playing this game. Maybe later missions turn out to be more enjoyable. Not my piece of cake. Completely disappointing.

[Rating: 3/10] Some solid improvements over WELCOME TO, some minor setbacks. You're essentially getting 8 games in one box. Granted, those eight games are variations of a theme, but of those versions at least 5 of them are markedly better than WELCOME TO, giving players more options and a larger decision space among which to operate.

[Rating: 3/10] Hugely disappointed with this one. The tediousness of the rules and campaign made me reach back for the original Welcome To.

[Rating: 3/10] This was my first experience with a flip-and-write and it cemented what I already knew: this sort of game is not for me. True multiplayer solitaire with no interaction at all other than racing others to score things first, since you all pick from the options at the same time there isn't any kind of way to hinder eachother. I felt nothing but worry that it wouldn't end soon enough and I'd miss the chance to play something engaging afterwards.

[Rating: 3/10] Way more complicated and fiddly than the original. Not every game needs a campaign mode, and "welcome to" definitely did not need a campaign. Just play the base game.

[Rating: 3/10] Welcome to Your Perfect Home is one of my favorite roll & write/draw & write games. It had straight forward concrete rules, a good rulebook, and measurable goals that keep gameplay achieveable for beginners but focused for the advanced.  This game has next to none of this. Breaking the game into several different ones is the quantity over quality feel. Rules are abstract and feel made up on the fly as if made by a child.
